title: 10 Best BigQuery Dashboard & Visualization Tools In 2026
summary: The 10 best BigQuery dashboard tools in 2026, from Data Studio and Looker to Metabase and GetDot: how each connects, what it costs, and how to cap query spend.
body_markdown:
## How I compared them


On BigQuery, four things decide how a dashboard tool behaves: **identity** (does every query run as one shared service account or as each viewer, which decides whether BigQuery's permissions apply per person and whether you can see who spent what), **acceleration** (can BI Engine serve it from memory), **cost controls** (byte caps, pre-aggregation, scheduled refresh), and **price** . The facts come from each vendor's documentation and pricing pages, linked in each section. I haven't benchmarked dashboard speed, so there are no speed rankings. Dot is our product; its section sticks to what our changelog and integration pages publicly describe.


## 1. Data Studio (formerly Looker Studio)


Google renamed Looker Studio back to Data Studio in April 2026 ([Google's announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/looker-studio-is-data-studio) , dated April 10); existing reports, data sources and users moved over with no action needed. Looker, the enterprise BI platform, keeps its name.


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a native connector. Each data source uses either owner's credentials (viewers see data through the owner's access and need no BigQuery permissions) or viewer's credentials (every viewer needs their own access) ([Google's connector docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/connect-to-google-bigquery) ). BI Engine can accelerate Data Studio reports ([BI Engine guide for Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bi-engine-looker-studio) ).


**Pricing:** free.[Data Studio Pro](https://cloud.google.com/datastudio) lists at $9 per user per project per month (the rate varies with subscription length) and adds team workspaces, organization-owned content and AI features.


**Limits:** unless you point it at a Looker model through the[Looker connector](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/limits-of-the-looker-connector) , calculated fields live in each data source, so two reports can define revenue two ways. With owner's credentials, every viewer sees whatever the owner can see. Every chart load and filter change is a query your project pays for, and BI Engine does not accelerate tables that use row-level security. If you're outgrowing it, see[Looker Studio alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-studio-alternatives) .


## 2. Looker


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account, or OAuth so each person queries as themselves (persistent derived tables then need an additional service account). LookML defines each metric once, PDTs and aggregate awareness pre-aggregate heavy queries, and the connection's **Max Billing Gigabytes** setting caps how much a query may scan ([Looker's BigQuery connection docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/db-config-google-bigquery) ,[Fivetran's Looker setup guide](https://fivetran.com/docs/destinations/bigquery/managed-bigquery/looker-setup-guide) ). BI Engine's SQL interface supports Looker.


**Pricing:** quote only: a platform fee plus Developer, Standard and Viewer licenses across Standard, Enterprise and Embed editions, on annual commitments, with BigQuery compute billed separately ([Google's Looker pricing page](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ). Our[Looker pricing breakdown](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-pricing) collects what third parties report it costs.


**Limits:** you need people who write LookML, the platform fee puts it out of reach for most small teams, and dashboards still only answer questions someone has modeled.


## 3. Power BI


**How it connects to BigQuery:** the Google BigQuery connector in Power Query, in Import or DirectQuery mode. Microsoft recommends its newer Arrow Database Connectivity (ADBC) implementation over the legacy ODBC one for new workloads, noting it may need extra BigQuery permissions ([connector docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/google-bigquery) ), and its[ADBC transition plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/transition-to-adbc) lists October 2026 as the planned start of making it the default, in phases. BI Engine's SQL interface supports Power BI.


**Pricing:** Pro is $14 per user per month and Premium Per User $24, both billed annually, after Microsoft's April 2025 increase ([DashboardFox](https://dashboardfox.com/blog/real-cost-microsoft-power-bi/) ). Large audiences move to Fabric capacity.


**Limits:** Import mode is only as fresh as the last scheduled refresh. DirectQuery sends visuals' queries to BigQuery as people use the report, with a 4-minute timeout per query in the Power BI service ([DirectQuery guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-directquery-about) ). Per-user licensing adds up when many people only view.


## 4. Tableau


**How it connects to BigQuery:** the Google BigQuery (JDBC) connector, live or as an extract. Tableau Desktop signs in with a service account key file or OAuth; Tableau's help lists only OAuth for Tableau Cloud. The "Use Storage API" option speeds up extracts but needs BigQuery read-session permissions ([Tableau's BigQuery JDBC help](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_googlebigquery_jdbc.htm) ). Google documents[BI Engine with Tableau](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bi-engine-sql-tableau) .


**Pricing:** Standard edition Creator $75, Explorer $42 and Viewer $15 per user per month; Enterprise edition $115, $70 and $35; billed annually. These are third-party figures ([DashboardFox](https://dashboardfox.com/guides/bi-software-pricing-guide/tableau-pricing-explained/) ).


**Limits:** extracts go stale between refreshes, and each refresh queries BigQuery; live connections send every interaction to BigQuery instead. Viewer seats add up for large audiences.


## 5. Metabase


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account with BigQuery Data Viewer, BigQuery Metadata Viewer and BigQuery Job User ([Metabase's BigQuery docs](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/databases/connections/bigquery) ). Google Cloud organizations created on or after May 3, 2024 block service account key creation by default, so you may need an org admin to allow a key.


**Pricing:** beyond the table, extra users cost $6 (Starter) or $12 (Pro), yearly billing lowers the plans to $90 and $517.50 a month, and Enterprise starts at $20,000 a year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing) ).


**Limits:** with the standard service-account connection, BigQuery sees every Metabase query as the same user, so per-person access and cost tracking live in Metabase, not in BigQuery.


## 6. Hex


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account; the BigQuery Storage API option speeds up large reads and needs the BigQuery Read Session User role. On Enterprise, admins can set up OAuth so each person queries with their own Google identity ([Hex's OAuth connection docs](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/data-connections/oauth-data-connections) ).


**Pricing:** Community is free; Professional is $36 and Team $75 per editor per month; Enterprise is custom, and larger compute is billed on usage ([Hex pricing](https://hex.tech/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** Hex is a notebook first, so the people building need SQL or Python.


## 7. Sigma


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account, or OAuth (beta) so queries and writes run under each user's own BigQuery permissions. Input tables write back to BigQuery; on an OAuth connection they still need a service account, which Sigma uses to log every edit, and dataset materializations aren't supported on OAuth ([Sigma's BigQuery docs](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/connect-to-bigquery) ).


**Limits:** Sigma sells on quotes, so you can't price it without a sales call, and write-back on a service-account connection means granting the BigQuery Data Editor role.


## 8. Apache Superset and Preset


**How it connects to BigQuery:** the` sqlalchemy-bigquery` driver, a connection string of` bigquery://{project_id}` , and a service account JSON key. Self-hosters should note that the BigQuery Python SDK isn't compatible with gevent, so use a different Gunicorn worker type ([Superset's BigQuery docs](https://superset.apache.org/user-docs/databases/supported/google-bigquery/) ).


**Pricing:** Preset Starter is free for up to 5 users, Professional is $25 billed monthly, and Enterprise is custom ([Preset pricing](https://preset.io/pricing/) ).


**Limits:** self-hosting means you own upgrades, caching and authentication, and someone technical usually sets up datasets before business users can build charts.


## 9. Evidence


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account that can run jobs and read your datasets, queried live; row-level security works through one service account per role with BigQuery row access policies ([Evidence's BigQuery docs](https://docs.evidence.dev/core-concepts/data-sources/bigquery) ).


**Pricing:** the framework is free under the MIT license. Evidence Studio, the hosted product, is sold on plans listed at[evidence.dev/pricing](https://evidence.dev/pricing) ; the figures I found in October 2026 contradicted each other, so I'm not quoting one.


**Limits:** every report is code, so business users read the reports but rarely build them.


## 10. GetDot: an AI analyst that answers and builds dashboards


Dot isn't a canvas you drag charts onto. People ask in Slack, Teams, email, the web app or an MCP client such as Claude ([Dot's MCP integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/mcp) ), and Dot writes the BigQuery SQL, runs it, and shows the SQL next to the answer. When an answer deserves to live on, you describe what you want to track and Dot builds the dashboard.


**How it connects to BigQuery:** a service account with read-only roles, and queries can run as each user, so BigQuery's own permissions and row-level security decide what each person sees. Dot reads nested and repeated fields, which matters for the GA4 export ([BigQuery integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/bigquery) ). Every query carries an audit stamp naming the user, the workspace and what triggered it, and on BigQuery the same facts land as job labels, so Dot's cost per user shows up in` INFORMATION_SCHEMA` and your billing export ([August 2026 changelog](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-08-01-answer-lineage) ). If you run Looker on BigQuery, Dot also answers from your explores, honoring their default filters ([Looker vs Dot](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/looker-vs-dot) ).


**Dashboards (Dot Apps):**


- Dot builds an interactive dashboard with KPIs, charts, tables and filters from a description, which you publish, share or embed ([March 2026](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-03-27-apps) ).
- Changing a filter re-runs only the queries that use it (August 2026), so fewer BigQuery scans per click.
- Dashboards can be marked Certified (July 2026) and sent on a schedule to email, Slack or Teams (September 2026).
- Dot can rebuild dashboards from Tableau, Power BI, Mixpanel, Metabase and Sigma and report any differences from the source (October 2026).


Apps are off by default while they roll out; an admin switches them on. At Emerge, the starting point was a dashboard problem: "We had nearly 50 different dashboards and none of them matched up," said Jeff Albenberg, their Director of Software Engineering ([case study](https://www.getdot.ai/impact/emerge) ). On Adyen's DABstep benchmark, a configured Dot answered 90% of the slice we ran ([our own result](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/from-10-to-90-percent-on-adyens-dabstep) ).


**Security:** Dot queries BigQuery in place without copying data, its LLM providers run with zero data retention, and it is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant, with SSO and role-based access.


**Pricing:** Free: $0 with 300 one-time credits and full Pro features. Pro: $180 a month billed annually ($200 month-to-month) with 150 credits a month. Team: $720 a month billed annually ($800 month-to-month) with 800 credits a month. Enterprise is custom. Every plan has unlimited users; you pay for credits (usage), not seats.


**Limits:** Dot is not a pixel-precise report designer, and questions and scheduled deliveries use credits, so heavy automated use needs a plan sized for it.


[Connect BigQuery and start free](https://app.getdot.ai/register) .


## What about AI and MCP on BigQuery?


Google runs a managed BigQuery MCP server that lets an assistant such as Claude or Cursor list tables and run SQL with your own Google login ([Google's BigQuery MCP docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp) ). It suits an engineer exploring data, but it isn't a dashboard tool: there are no shared metric definitions and nothing to publish. Our[BigQuery MCP guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/bigquery-mcp-server) covers setup and how it compares with Gemini in BigQuery.


## How to keep BigQuery costs down when dashboards query it


On-demand BigQuery bills $6.25 per TiB scanned after the first free TiB each month (list price as of October 2026,[BigQuery pricing](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) ), and a dashboard multiplies every scan by every chart, viewer and filter change. These are the levers, roughly in order of payoff.


### Partition big tables, and require a partition filter


Partitioning (usually by date) makes a query read only the partitions it filters on, and clustering lets BigQuery skip blocks when you filter on clustered columns ([Google's cost guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-costs) ). Requiring a partition filter makes an unfiltered query fail instead of scanning everything:


```text
CREATE TABLE analytics.events_partitioned
PARTITION BY DATE(event_timestamp)
CLUSTER BY customer_id, event_name
OPTIONS (require_partition_filter = TRUE)
AS SELECT * FROM analytics.events;
```


Cluster on the columns your dashboard filters use most, and give every dashboard a default date range.


### Turn on BI Engine for the dashboard project


BI Engine is an in-memory reservation you buy per project. When it accelerates a query, the stage that reads table data is billed as 0 bytes on-demand. The reservation costs $0.0416 per GiB per hour (about $30 a month per GiB, as of October 2026). Data Studio uses it natively, and its SQL interface extends it to Looker, Tableau, Power BI and other tools ([BigQuery pricing](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) ,[Google's BI Engine announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/bigquery-bi-engine-generally-available) ). It does not accelerate tables with row-level security, so plan acceleration and governance together.


### Cap bytes per query with maximum bytes billed


Set a maximum bytes billed on the queries a tool runs (Looker calls it Max Billing Gigabytes). If BigQuery's estimate exceeds the cap, the query fails without a charge; on clustered tables the estimate is an upper bound, so a query can fail even when the real scan would have fit.


```text
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --maximum_bytes_billed=10000000000 \
'SELECT country, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM analytics.orders
WHERE order_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
GROUP BY country'
```


For a ceiling across a whole project, custom quotas limit query bytes per day, per project or per user, as a safeguard rather than an exact limit ([custom quotas](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/custom-quotas) ).


### Pre-aggregate with materialized views


A materialized view keeps an aggregate current as the base table changes, and BigQuery's smart tuning rewrites matching queries on the base table to read an incremental view instead, so dashboards benefit without changing their SQL. Keep automatic refresh on; otherwise queries go back to the base tables once the view falls behind ([Google's materialized view docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/materialized-views-use) ).


```text
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW analytics.daily_revenue_mv
OPTIONS (enable_refresh = TRUE, refresh_interval_minutes = 60)
AS
SELECT DATE(order_ts) AS order_date, country, SUM(amount) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM analytics.orders
GROUP BY order_date, country;
```


### Find out which dashboard is spending the money


The` INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS` view records who ran each query and how many bytes it billed ([JOBS view docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/information-schema-jobs) ):


```text
SELECT
user_email,
COUNT(*) AS queries,
ROUND(SUM(total_bytes_billed) / POW(1024, 4), 2) AS tib_billed
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS
WHERE creation_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
AND job_type = 'QUERY'
GROUP BY user_email
ORDER BY tib_billed DESC
LIMIT 20;
```


A tool on one shared service account shows up as a single` user_email` : you learn the tool is expensive, not which dashboard or person. Per-user OAuth, or job labels (in the view's` labels` column), make that cost traceable.


If the dashboard is for leadership, what goes on it matters more than the tool; see how to build an executive dashboard. If some of your data lives in Postgres, see PostgreSQL reporting tools.
